label: Systematized Early Buddhist Abhidharma and Mahayana consciousness analysis
description: Vasubandhu synthesized centuries of Buddhist psychological analysis first in the Abhidharmakosa and then into Yogacara’s Consciousness-Only phenomenology.
dialecticalTension: Transforms early Buddhist no-self (anatman) analysis into a full theory of karmic subconsciousness.

label: Reinterpreted Madhyamaka emptiness through phenomenological consciousness-only analysis
description: Responding to Nagarjuna’s emptiness (sunyata), Vasubandhu grounded non-duality in the three natures (trisvabhava) and the eradication of subject-object bifurcation.
dialecticalTension: Shifts focus from Madhyamaka dialectical negation to phenomenological analysis of mental construction.

label: Formulated the eight-consciousness model centered on subliminal Alayavijnana
description: In the Thirty Verses (Trimsika), Vasubandhu explained how subliminal storehouse consciousness (alaya-vijnana) carries karmic seeds and projects dualistic appearance.
dialecticalTension: Explains continuity of memory, karma, and illusion without positing a substantial soul.

label: Transmitted East Asian Yogacara and Abhidharma foundations to Japanese Zen
description: Via Xuanzang’s Faxiang and Tiantai/Chan syntheses, Vasubandhu’s analysis of mind-only and non-dual realization informed Dogen’s Zen phenomenology of Mind and Buddha-nature.
dialecticalTension: Bridges Indian Yogacara epistemology to East Asian Zen non-duality.

label: Prefigured transcendental phenomenology’s reduction of outer objects to intentional consciousness
description: Contemporary comparative philosophers note deep structural resonances between Vasubandhu’s phenomenological epoche of external matter and Husserl’s intentional constitution.
dialecticalTension: Illuminates parallel anti-naturalist reductions across Indian Yogacara and European phenomenology.
